clue.text: The man's fear of Spain

parts.note: belonging to the man is his
panic is sudden fear

explanation.surface: A man's dread of the country of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Hispanic describes anything relating to Spain or Spanish-speaking peoples, an adjective like the phrase.

clue.text: Bully boy

explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to bully, and Hector is also a boy's name.

clue.text: Fool's easy to name

parts.note: simple means easy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fool is a pushover to identify.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool's' is read as 'Fool is', with the definition first.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is a foolish, gullible person.

clue.text: Article's quite new — not this then

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: new means the letters of quite are made anew in a fresh order

explanation.surface: This piece looks quite fresh, so it cannot be old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges QUITE to TIQUE. The definition plays on the clue: something antique is not new.
explanation.definitionFit: An antique is old, so it is the opposite of new, which the clue's 'this' refers to.

clue.text: Silly screwy son sacked

indicators.note: sacked means the son is dismissed from the word

parts.note: screwy means crazy, insane

explanation.surface: A foolish, crazy boy has been fired.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or senseless.

clue.text: Dash off short piece extremely well

indicators.note: short means the word for piece loses its final letter

parts.note: a scrap is a small piece

indicators.note: extremely points to the outermost letters of the following word

explanation.surface: Writing a brief piece very nicely in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims SCRAP to SCRA; 'extremely' takes W and L, the ends of 'well'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrawl is to write hurriedly and messily, which is dashing something off.

clue.text: Bore merit

definitions.meaning: the internal diameter of a gun barrel
quality or worth of a person

explanation.definitionFit: Calibre means both a gun's bore and a person's quality or worth.

clue.text: Revise table, they say

indicators.note: they say signals a word spoken aloud with the same sound

parts.note: an altar is a table in a church

explanation.surface: Edit a table, people suggest.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter is to change, as in revising.

clue.text: Note attached to cheek cosmetic

indicators.note: attached to joins the note after the cheek word

parts.note: lip is cheeky talk
a gloss is an explanatory note

explanation.surface: A memo attached to the face about make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheek and lip both mean insolence here, not parts of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip gloss is a cosmetic giving lips a shiny finish.

clue.text: Maybe Hereford mist shrouds river and pond dweller

parts.note: a Hereford is a breed of cattle, so a bull is an example

indicators.note: shrouds means the mist wraps round the river letter

parts.note: fog is thick mist

explanation.surface: Fog hides a stream and a cow-like creature living by a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: Hereford is an English cattle breed as well as a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfrog is a large frog that lives in and around ponds.

clue.text: Woke up before a period ended

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the rest

parts.note: to come to is to regain consciousness
period is the American term for the punctuation mark a full stop

explanation.surface: Someone woke up just before a spell of time ran out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Period' looks like a span of time, but it is the punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to a full stop is an idiom meaning to halt or finish completely.

clue.text: Devious slash

explanation.definitionFit: Oblique means indirect or devious, and is also the name for the slash mark.

clue.text: Generous artist included in defamatory publication

indicators.note: included in places the artist inside the publication word

parts.note: a libel is a published defamatory statement
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A generous painter is named in a libellous article.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal means giving freely, a synonym of generous.

clue.text: Vessel carrying right flag

indicators.note: carrying means the vessel holds the next piece within it

parts.note: a steamer is a steam-powered ship

explanation.surface: A ship flying the proper banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow flag or pennant.

clue.text: Anchor at sea in my domain

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word my

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of anchor are mixed up

explanation.surface: Dropping anchor in waters I control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges ANCHOR to ONARCH, which goes 'in' MY.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarchy is a kingdom, a realm or domain ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Guiding beliefs in Soviet hospitals

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: The principles underlying medical care in the USSR.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside 'Soviet hospitals', where the run spans the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the characteristic spirit or set of guiding beliefs of a group.

clue.text: Person in charge on ship is a star

parts.note: a head is the person in charge
a liner is a passenger ship

explanation.surface: The captain on board is a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: A headliner is the star act or performer topping a bill.

clue.text: 'Tass', long spreading a Gorbachev initiative

indicators.note: spreading means the letters of the two words spread out in a new order

explanation.surface: The Soviet news agency, long spreading a reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' rearranges TASS and LONG. Tass was the Soviet news agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasnost, openness, was Mikhail Gorbachev's policy of transparency in the USSR.

clue.text: Comic strip character, duck, backing America

indicators.note: backing means the word for duck is turned round

parts.note: a duck is a score of nil in cricket
US is America

explanation.surface: A cartoon character, a duck, supporting the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses NIL to LIN. A duck in cricket is a score of zero; Linus is the blanket-carrying boy in Peanuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Linus van Pelt is a character in the Peanuts comic strip.

clue.text: Drink wine got from base

parts.note: to sup is to drink
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Drink wine taken from a stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A support is a base or foundation that holds something up.

clue.text: Ornate thing by grate, a nocturnal bird

indicators.note: ornate suggests elaborate rearranging, so the word thing is reshuffled

parts.note: to grate on someone is to jar

explanation.surface: A decorative object next to the fireplace, and a bird that flies at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ornate' rearranges THING to NIGHT. 'Grate' looks like a fireplace but is the verb meaning to jar.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightjar is a bird that feeds and calls at dusk and night.

clue.text: Creeping plant in house on wheels

definitions.meaning: a plant that trails along the ground

explanation.definitionFit: A trailer is a trailing plant and, in America, a caravan or mobile home.

clue.text: In the existing circumstances, arsenic may be used on Italian island

parts.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
It is short for Italian, as in vermouth

explanation.surface: Poison could be used on an island in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: As it is means given the situation as it stands now.

clue.text: Scuttle in small holidaymaker's van?

parts.note: a camper is a van fitted out for holidays

explanation.surface: Scurrying about inside a little camper van?
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to run quickly with small steps, as to scuttle.

clue.text: Saw a duke grow old

parts.note: to age is to grow old

explanation.surface: Watched an aristocrat getting older.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying, a proverb or adage.

clue.text: Medical complaint, chronic fatigue syndrome, affected sales

parts.note: ME, myalgic encephalomyelitis, is another name for chronic fatigue syndrome

indicators.note: affected means the word sales is disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: An illness causing exhaustion has hit a firm's sales figures.
explanation.walkthrough: ME, the British name for chronic fatigue syndrome, is a crossword staple; 'affected' looks like describing the firm but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Measles is an infectious viral illness, a medical complaint.

clue.text: Injures top of head in swamp

parts.note: mars means damages or spoils

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of head in this down entry

explanation.surface: A blow to the head in boggy ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A marsh is low-lying waterlogged land, a swamp.

clue.text: Flying separately, ahead of time, with one's head in the clouds

definitions.text: with one's head in the clouds

indicators.note: ahead of puts the first piece before the next

parts.note: travelling by air apart from someone is being on a different aircraft

explanation.surface: Travelling by different flights, early, while daydreaming.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for flying apart, 'on another plane', gains T to become the idiom for being out of touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on another planet is an idiom for being dreamy and out of touch, like having one's head in the clouds.

clue.text: Handle party at last in negotiation

parts.note: to handle someone is to treat them

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of party

explanation.surface: Managing a gathering finally in talks.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is an agreement reached by negotiation; it can also mean the negotiating itself.

clue.text: French city residence briefly shown on map

indicators.note: shown on places the shortened residence after the map in this across entry

parts.note: a chart is a map
res is a short form of residence

explanation.surface: A home marked on a chart in brief.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartres is a cathedral city in France.
